es: Redactar una anécdota con escena de fondo, hecho que la rompe, giro con was about to / was going to y desenlace con would (Little did I know…).

teaching.en: The café was nearly empty, and the rain was tapping on the windows.
teaching.es: El café estaba casi vacío y la lluvia golpeteaba las ventanas.
teaching.explanationEs: Past continuous para el fondo de la escena: was tapping.

teaching.en: Suddenly, a woman sat down at my table.

teaching.explanationEs: Suddenly + past simple: el hecho que rompe la escena.

teaching.en: I was about to pay when I realised my wallet was gone.
teaching.es: Iba a pagar cuando me di cuenta de que mi cartera había desaparecido.
teaching.explanationEs: Was about to + verbo base: estaba a punto de; se interrumpe con un hecho en past simple.
segments: I was about to pay when
I realised my wallet was gone.
teaching.audioText: I was about to pay when I realised my wallet was gone.

teaching.en: I was going to call the police, but then the woman smiled and handed me my wallet.

teaching.explanationEs: Was going to + verbo: intención en el pasado que no se cumple; but then introduce el giro.
segments: I was going to call the police, but then
the woman smiled and handed me my wallet.
teaching.audioText: I was going to call the police, but then the woman smiled and handed me my wallet.

teaching.en: Little did I know that she would become my business partner.
teaching.es: Yo no tenía ni idea de que se convertiría en mi socia.
teaching.explanationEs: Little al inicio pide inversión (did I know) y would anticipa el desenlace.

teaching.audioText: Little did I know that she would become my business partner.

teaching.en: The twist was that she had found my wallet under the table an hour earlier.
teaching.es: El giro fue que había encontrado mi cartera debajo de la mesa una hora antes.
teaching.explanationEs: El giro cambia lo que el lector creía; had found sitúa lo ocurrido antes.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de unas 130 palabras con escena, giro y desenlace.

answer.text: It was a cold night, and the rain was falling on the roof of the bus station. The waiting room was almost empty, and a tired man was sleeping on a bench. I was about to buy a ticket when I realised my wallet was gone. Suddenly, my hands began to tremble. I was going to call my brother, but then a stranger walked over and handed me some money. "Take it," he said. "You can pay me back tomorrow." I thanked him and took the last bus home. Little did I know that I would see him again. The following week, he walked into my first job interview. He was the manager, and he would become my boss for the next five years.
accepted: It was a cold night, and the rain was falling on the roof of the bus station. The waiting room was almost empty, and a tired man was sleeping on a bench. I was about to buy a ticket when I realised my wallet was gone. Suddenly, my hands began to tremble. I was going to call my brother, but then a stranger walked over and handed me some money. "Take it," he said. "You can pay me back tomorrow." I thanked him and took the last bus home. Little did I know that I would see him again. The following week, he walked into my first job interview. He was the manager, and he would become my boss for the next five years.

It was a rainy evening, and the wind was blowing hard outside the station. A few people were waiting quietly in the dark. I was about to get on the last bus when I realised my wallet was not in my bag. My heart was beating very fast. I was going to ask the driver for help, but a young woman gave me a ticket. "Don't worry," she said. "Buy me a coffee one day." I thanked her and sat by the window. Little did I know that I would meet her again. Two weeks later, she came into my new office, and she would become my best friend for the rest of my life.

feedback.es: Una buena anécdota abre con una escena en pasado continuo, la rompe con un hecho, usa was about to / was going to y anticipa el final con would (Little did I know…).

origin.text: Situación: una noche de lluvia en la estación de autobuses. Ibas a comprar un billete cuando te diste cuenta de que no tenías la cartera. Ibas a llamar a tu hermano, pero un desconocido te dio dinero. Giro: más tarde volviste a verlo.
